comments.text: lei: "unique when present (P1)" reads as a rule but did not parse, so the platform would enforce nothing. A notes cell holds one rule per ";" clause — move the explanation into a clause of its own: "format(20 alphanumeric); why it is required".

text: R1: WHEN a legal entity is saved with an LEI that another non-retired entity already carries, the system SHALL reject the save. (Uniqueness scope: active + draft; a retired entity's LEI may not be re-used by a new entity.)

comments.text: R1's WHEN clause only covers an LEI held by "another non-retired entity", but the parenthetical adds "a retired entity's LEI may not be re-used by a new entity" — a case the WHEN clause does not reject. Meanwhile P1 ("unique across the register when present") is absolute and the platform will enforce it against retired rows too, so the requirement text contradicts the enforced behaviour. Either widen R1's WHEN clause to cover any existing entity (making the parenthetical redundant) or drop the parenthetical and state that retired-row reuse is rejected by P1; as written, an implementer reading only R1 would permit reuse of a retired LEI, and A1 does not test that case either.

text: P3: a retired legal entity is immutable except for its status and retirement date.

comments.text: P3 and A4 permit editing a retired entity's status and retiredOn — but the only meaningful status edit on a retired row is reinstating it to active/draft, and no requirement defines reinstatement. If reactivation is intended, it needs a requirement (does the entity re-enter R2's new-business selection? what happens if its LEI was re-used in the meantime — though P1 makes that impossible, which itself means a retired LEI permanently blocks reuse, worth confirming is wanted). If reactivation is NOT intended, say so, because as written the spec silently allows a retired entity to be flipped back to active with no rule governing it.

text: R2: WHEN a legal entity is retired, the system SHALL exclude it from selection for new trades, new agreements and any other new business, while keeping the record and all references to it intact.

comments.text: R2 requires exclusion from "new trades, new agreements and any other new business", but trade booking and the agreement stack are both declared OUT of scope — this register cannot enforce behaviour in flows it does not specify. What the register actually controls is its own selection surface (the picker other specs consume). Consider restating R2 in terms the register owns — e.g. a retired entity is excluded from the register's selection/picker — and noting that consuming specs must honour it, otherwise acceptance of R2 depends on systems this spec explicitly excludes.
